problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=y(x-3)^{3}.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>0$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ |  |  |
|  | $x<3$ | $x>3$ |

feedback.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=(x+1)^{2}(y-2).$ Fill in the missing signs in the sign table of $f(x,y)$ shown below.

| $y>2$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<2$ | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |
|  | $x<-1$ | $x>-1$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=-1$ and $y=2.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/bce3befee4d7ae90df59b7bfb17e965ca29615220ca6845a78cfaad3e02a0730.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/b6cac24748d4a3990038ef7140943bd0947207456132e66ca6b7fb887be44164.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x+1)^{2}$ | $(y-2)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-2,3)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(0,3)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-2,1)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(0,1)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/174965ef064b55b29326c4681f709a6dfcbc690673e2e5a7498e9a65c4a6af2c.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>2$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<2$ | $-$ | $-$ |
|  | $x<-1$ | $x>-1$ |
